title: TSA/FBI Facial Match — Viktor Sorin Identified

caller.name: Special Agent D. Rivas, FBI Cyber Division
caller.label: FBI

transcript.speaker: FBI
transcript.text: Security Officer Teller, this is Special Agent D. Rivas, FBI Cyber Division. We’ve just run your CCTV still from Door S-4 through Interpol’s facial recognition database. We have a potential match: Viktor Sorin, 34, Ukrainian national, flagged as a known associate of a cybercrime-as-a-service operation based in Eastern Europe. He’s not on any terrorist watchlist, but he’s been linked to multiple network intrusions via rogue hardware implants. We believe Sorin was hired to establish persistent access to your network. He installed the device in Electrical Room B. The client — whoever paid him — now has the means to reach your network from outside, including the parking structure. If that rogue AP is still broadcasting, they may already be on your network. Or they may not have connected yet. Either way, whoever hired Sorin now knows how to get in. We recommend immediate isolation of Port 23 on the Cisco 2960 switch. Do not reboot the switch. Preserve logs.

transcript.speaker: SEC
transcript.text: Understood, Agent Rivas. We’re already on it. We’ve confirmed the device is still active. We’ll isolate Port 23 and begin containment. Will keep you updated.

voiceStyles.FBI: Male, mid-40s, calm, authoritative, background low-frequency hum
voiceStyles.SEC: Female, late 20s, urgent, professional, slight static

instructorNote: This inject triggers the critical containment decision. The team must now decide whether to disconnect the rogue AP (stop lateral movement) or leave it running to catch the client. FBI's direction is to isolate, but the team must weigh intelligence value against risk.
